title: test(cli): cut per-spawn cost in five migrate integration suites (#23181 slice 12)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XAViUhQDMdVeNR9YVhJW1y5)_

Part of #23181 (slice 12, claim 6417640032). The card stays open: this PR cuts real work in five of the eight `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/*.integration.test.ts` rows, and closes none of the 10 s rows outright. The routes that could close them are in "Not taken" below.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

`skip-changeset`: a test-only diff. The five files are `*.integration.test.ts` under `packages/cli/src/`, and `@objectstack/cli` publishes `files: [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md]`; the build program does not compile test files.

## The reading used

The newest refresh with a per-file list is PR #25960 (14 hourly full-battery runs, `measure-test-shard-timings --diff`); #26089 landed from the same list. This family's rows in it, CI wall per file:

| file | CI s (run) | spawns of the CLI per file |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `data-commands.absent-database` | 394.05 (`40200279306`) | 43 CLI + 2 seed boots |
| `object-scope` | 180.37 (`40204927516`) | 18 CLI + 1 seed + 17 reader/writer children |
| `plan.boot-parity` | 118.02 (`40204927516`) | 6, through tsx |
| `plan.telemetry-sibling` | 113.36 (`40200279306`) | 5, through tsx |
| `unmapped-columns` | 98.92 (`40204927516`) | 10 CLI + 1 seed + 2 reader children |
| `plan.declared-default-datasource` | 95.65 (declared 80) | 4, through tsx |
| `plan.nullable-tenant-columns` | 62.72 (`40204927516`) | 4 (1 serve boot, 3 plans), through tsx |
| `resume.recorded-by` | 43.98 (`40200279306`) | 4 crash children + 2 serve boots, resume in-process |

The family's ninth row, `plan.deferred-reads` (18.22 s), is left for a later slice: the claim caps a slice at about 8 files.

## Mechanism: the order's hypothesis does not hold here

The order's usual shape, a per-case boot, is not present. Every file already builds its fixture once, in a `beforeAll` it owns or in a case that owns its fixture alone. Each file's cost is the number of CLI spawns times the per-spawn floor, run one after another. On this box (4 cores, idle, inside the verify lock):

- `node bin/run-dev.js --version`: 4.93 to 4.99 s; `migrate resume --json` on an absent database: 5.25 to 6.06 s.
- `tsx bin/run-dev.js --version`: 8.28 to 8.44 s; the same `migrate resume`: 9.35 to 10.09 s.
- One `node -e` child that opens the database with `driver-sql` and reads it: 0.45 to 0.54 s.

Most of the 5 s floor is oclif importing every command from `src/`, because no `oclif.manifest.json` ships for the source entry. That is product code and outside this claim.

## What changed

1. **Four files spawn the source entry with this process's `node`, not the `tsx` binary** (`plan.boot-parity`, `plan.telemetry-sibling`, `plan.declared-default-datasource`, `plan.nullable-tenant-columns`). The entry (`bin/run-dev.js`), its `src/` and the `NODE_ENV=development` it pins are unchanged. This is how the family's other spawners already spawn it (`data-commands.absent-database`, `object-scope`, `unmapped-columns`, and `resume.recorded-by` for `serve`). The `tsx` wrapper added a second process and its own transform, about 3.4 s per spawn. Fixture configs still load through the CLI's own `bundle-require`. `vitest-tiers.ts` still files all four as integration (they value-import `node:child_process` and name `run-dev`).
2. **`object-scope` reads and writes its fixture database in-process** through `better-sqlite3`, as `plan.boot-parity` and `plan.telemetry-sibling` already do. It used one `node` child per read: 16 `readState` calls and 1 off-shape write. Each query is the same column list and `ORDER BY id`, and the connection is opened read-write as knex opened it.

Every assertion is unchanged. The diff touches no `expect`, no case and no timeout.

## Measured

Same box, before (`a335f1de`) and after (`54d51cc3`), N=3 per file, one file per `vitest run --project integration --maxWorkers=1` under `os-verify-lock`. These are process wall and user CPU, which include the hook (the JSON reporter's per-file time leaves out `beforeAll`).

| file | before wall s (3 runs) | after wall s (3 runs) | median change | user CPU s, medians |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|:--|
| `plan.boot-parity` | 63.16 · 67.17 · 63.06 | 40.54 · 37.84 · 41.89 | −36% | 87.5 → 56.2 |
| `plan.telemetry-sibling` | 64.47 · 67.21 · 62.03 | 53.08 · 38.21 · 42.63 | −34% | 89.6 → 58.4 |
| `plan.declared-default-datasource` | 63.37 · 63.40 · 63.33 | 48.20 · 47.17 · 51.16 | −24% | 89.4 → 69.3 |
| `plan.nullable-tenant-columns` | 42.54 · 42.74 · 42.72 | 28.34 · 29.28 · 27.87 | −34% | 59.2 → 39.1 |
| `object-scope` | 108.79 · 117.71 · 112.76 | 106.64 · 100.00 · 105.03 | −7% | 157.6 → 149.4 |

CPU falls with wall, so this is work removed, not work packed.

**Projection, not proof.** Scaling by each file's own CI-to-local ratio (CI reading ÷ local before-median): `plan.declared-default-datasource` ≈ 73 s, under its declared 80 s budget, so the next refresh should stop listing it. That is the one row this PR is expected to close. The others project to `plan.boot-parity` ≈ 76 s, `plan.telemetry-sibling` ≈ 75 s, `plan.nullable-tenant-columns` ≈ 42 s and `object-scope` ≈ 168 s, all still over 10 s.

**Isolation.** Two shuffled runs of the five files, all green:
- `--sequence.shuffle --sequence.seed=23181`: 5/5 files, 27/27 tests.
- `--sequence.seed=7` with an execution-order reporter: file order nullable → boot-parity → object-scope → declared-default → telemetry, and `object-scope`'s 20 cases ran out of definition order; 27/27 passed.

The hook files' cases only read what a hook recorded. `plan.boot-parity` and `plan.telemetry-sibling` build a fresh `mkdtemp` fixture per case.

## Not taken: the routes that would close the remaining rows

None of these is inside the claim. They are open questions on the card for the seat.

- **A. Spawn the built entry (`bin/run.js`).** Its floor was measured at 2.46 to 2.66 s against 5.45 to 6.07 s (`vitest.config.ts`); slice 9 reads 2.7 to 3.0 against 10.0 to 10.3 s. It changes the `NODE_ENV` posture and makes `dist/` a prerequisite, so it needs a ruling. Slice 9 raises the same question.
- **B. Run a file's independent spawns concurrently.** Measured on `data-commands.absent-database` (a local experiment, not committed): pool 1 → 263.1 s wall, 431.9 s CPU; pool 2 → 152.4 s, 422.5 s; pool 4 → 120.7 s, 433.4 s. Wall falls while CPU stays flat, so this packs the work rather than removing it. `vitest.config.ts` rejects the same trade for `maxWorkers` because it spends cores that belong to the shard.
- **C. A declared budget** (ruling record 6181973363 letter B, class "spawns the real producer once per single-cause fixture"). `plan.declared-default-datasource` and `audit-mail-bodies.archive` in this directory already use it. It conflicts with the card's "runs under 10 s".

## Gates

All at head `54d51cc3d`.

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 58 commands over the 5-path change set. Each one's exit code was captured by redirecting, then reading `$?`, with no pipe. **All 58 exit 0.** `--ran`: "Run reconciliation — 58 derived, 58 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", exit 0.
- Six gates first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET), and all six exit 0 on re-run: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (shallow clone; fixed by fetching its positive control `621a4876`), and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:i18n-walk-parity`, `check:type-check-debt` (no built `dist/`; fixed by a full `turbo run build`, 121/121 tasks).
- `eslint --no-inline-config packages/cli`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` + `check:test-typecheck`): `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- The five files, `vitest run --project integration` (the integration tier is this diff's own layer): 5/5 files and 27/27 tests in every run above (3 ordered runs and 2 shuffled).
- `packages/cli/dist` after the build contains no test file (`dist/commands/migrate` has 0 `*.test.*`).

## Acceptance notes

- `unmapped-columns` has the same reader-child shape (2 children, about 1 s of its about 99 s). It is left as it is: its readers compare BLOB-carrying rows byte for byte, which is not worth the risk for one second.
- `data-commands.absent-database`, `unmapped-columns` and `resume.recorded-by` already spawn through `node`. Inside this claim their only lever is B, which is not taken.
